clinician.trajectory_summary: A 60-year-old man with HIV, remote hepatitis C, diabetes mellitus type II, and prior Hodgkin's lymphoma presented with altered mental status. On admission, he had stable vitals but exhibited bilateral anterior cervical lymphadenopathy, left inguinal lymphadenopathy, diffuse rhonchi on respiratory exam, and a grade 3 systolic murmur. Laboratory studies revealed pancytopenia, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, acute kidney injury, and lactic acidosis. Imaging studies (CT abdomen) demonstrated moderate splenomegaly and multiple enlarged lymph nodes (left cardiophrenic, retrocrural, celiac, mesenteric, portacaval, aortocaval, and iliac). CT head showed no acute intracranial process; chest X-ray revealed right lung base airspace opacity concerning for pneumonia. Lymph node aspiration demonstrated EBV-EBER-positive, CD30-positive cells with a mixed immunophenotype (LCA, BOB-1, CD79a, PAX-5, CD68 positive; ALK, CD20, CD3, OCT2, HHV8 negative) consistent with Hodgkin lymphoma. Pathology confirmed the presence of necrosis, diagnosing grade III LyG. Treatment with brentuximab/bendamustine was initiated, and the patient was discharged hemodynamically stable to follow up with Oncology as an outpatient.
